subject: Retain names generated in function calls

messages.author: 9c9b5f9c6aaa025d
messages.subject: Retain names generated in function calls
parts:
Hello,
I learned a while ago, from Hadley in one of his classes if I remember correctly, to avoid `sapply` in favor of `vapply` because of `sapply`'s possibility of returning a result of an unexpected type. In other words, it is safer to state explicitly what you want your values casted to using `vapply`.

I currently have a situation where I have an unnamed vector of values to which I want to apply a function. The nuance here that is mixing me up is that my function returns a named numeric. When I use `sapply`, the name is retained. When I use `vapply`, it is not. I turned to `plyr` for help hoping `laply` would retain the names, but it acts just like `vapply`. The only `plyr` solution I came up with was using a combination of `unlist` and `llply`, which I don't think is ideal. See code below for examples.

My instinct is that `laply` should retain the names. Or am I missing something here that I could do this all in one function call (but not using `sapply`)? Or should I just rework my code to avoid the structure/situation all-together?

Many thanks,
Doug

###
foo <- function(x){ names(x) <- paste0("foo.", x); return(x); }
values <- 1:3;

### Base R
sapply(values, foo);
# foo.1 foo.2 foo.3
# 1 2 3
vapply(values, foo, numeric(1));
# [1] 1 2 3

### plyr
library(plyr);
laply(values, foo);
# [1] 1 2 3
unlist(llply(values, foo));
# foo.1 foo.2 foo.3
# 1 2 3
